title: ER diagram on ELK: Mermaid's block order and directions, rounded relationships with line hops

v:
## Context

The ER diagram moves onto the shared ELK layout core (`layout/directedGraph/`), the fourth and last kind after the flowchart (`01M4VA67HYZZ1PZG49XA30454N`), the class diagram (`01M4VHSY2W1Q9E5QCA51F1TCJM`) and the state diagram (`01M4VKTJ2A1DGXAMYVF16BK2W3`), under the rules of `01M4VANRC6B2C14NHVC2KRZ9Y8`. On dagre the ER adapter grew every block's frame itself (`subgraphFrames`, a union with the members because the dagre core handed a nested cluster back at its given size) and shifted the drawing to hold frames that grew past the engine's extent; relationships were `basis` curves.

What Mermaid 12.2.0 does, read in its dist (`node_modules/.pnpm/mermaid@12.2.0/node_modules/mermaid/dist/chunks/mermaid.esm/`) and measured in headless Chrome:

- **Handover order.** `ErDB.getData` (`erDiagram-VZDIDQZ7.mjs`, line 1340) lists every block before any entity, walking `subGraphs` backwards; the parser records a block when it reduces its `end` (line 189), so that list is in closing order and the walk puts a parent before its children and the last sibling first. Then every entity in the entity table's insertion order (first mention), then every relationship in source order. The ELK adapter (`elk-V4PLJRSU.mjs`) builds each level's children in that order (`addVertices`); `orderNodesForElkPaint` reorders only after layout, for painting. Measured: `subgraph SA { A }`, `subgraph SB { B }`, `X` draws SB, SA, X left to right; `subgraph O { subgraph I1 { A }, subgraph I2 { B }, C }` draws C, I2, I1 inside O. The flowchart's `FlowDB.getData` does the same. (The dagre adapter handed blocks over before entities too, but in opening order.)
- **Blocks.** A block is an ELK compound node with `dir` only when its body wrote `direction` (`getData`, `dir: subGraph.dir`), through the same `configureSubgraphNodes` / `configureCrossHierarchyEdges` as the flowchart. Measured: `subgraph outer { direction LR; subgraph inner { A ||--o{ B : r }; C }` draws A and B side by side in one row (inner laid out in outer's pass; Mermaid 11 on dagre stacked them in the document's `TB`); `subgraph sales { direction LR; CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER : places }` with `WAREHOUSE` keeps the row; adding `ORDER ||--|{ LINE-ITEM : contains` from outside stacks CUSTOMER above ORDER.
- **Relationship labels.** Each relationship is an edge with one inline `CENTER` label (`addEdgesToElkGraph`, line 99805; `labelpos: "c"` from `getData`) — the flowchart's construction, which the core already ports. Measured on `er-subgraphs`: every label's centre lies on its route (0.1 to 2.6px off, at 28% to 70% of the route's length), the self-relationship's 20px beside its loop; Siren's land at the same fractions (0.1 to 3.9px off), its self-relationship's 29px beside the loop.
- **Cardinality markers.** Each end carries its own start or end marker (`arrowTypeStart` / `arrowTypeEnd`); every route ELK makes is drawn `rounded` (`applyElkEdgeLayout`, line 100401, overriding `getData`'s `curve: "basis"`), so a route's first and last runs are straight and each marker lies along its run. Measured on `er-subgraphs`: every end leaves its box along the same axis on both sides — vertical on six relationships, horizontal, out and back, on the self-relationship.
- **Line hops** on every relationship, as on the other kinds' connectors.

## Decision

The ER adapter (`layoutErDiagram`) hands the core every block as a cluster (12px padding, the title's measured size, the block's direction when it wrote one) in Mermaid's order (`mermaidBlockOrder`: the opening-order list walked children-first, reversed), then every entity in the model's order (first mention, Mermaid's), then every relationship in the model's order with its measured label and the `rounded` corner radius (`ER_CONNECTOR_CURVE`). `subgraphFrames` and the shift are gone; frames, loops, label anchors, title placement and the extent are the core's. The ER renderer draws relationships `rounded` with the layout's hops; the markers are unchanged (`orient="auto-start-reverse"` follows the first and last runs).

No departure from Mermaid 12 was needed, and the core gained no capability.

Measured, no change: relationship labels in a block's title band. An ER relationship has only a centre label (its cardinalities are markers, not text), and ELK places a centre label in a layer, never in a band. Over the ER parity fixtures, both measurers, and twelve documents built to provoke it (a label on each relationship entering or leaving a block, nested blocks, relationships into an inner block from outside, a member related to its sibling, each in TB, LR, BT and RL), no relationship label reached a block's title band. So labels are not added to the title's obstacles (`placeTitlesClear`), as for the state diagram.

## Evidence

Gate (rule 8 of `01M4VANRC6B2C14NHVC2KRZ9Y8`), parity over the four ER fixtures (`example-er-core`, `er-long-labels`, `example-er-reveal`, `er-subgraphs`), Siren against Mermaid 12.2.0 default in headless Chrome:

| Measure | Siren on ELK | Siren on dagre (before) | Mermaid | Gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Through unrelated boxes | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Crossings | 0 | 0 | 0 | at most 110% of Mermaid's |
| Vertical agreement (pooled, 36 pairs) | 97.2% | 58.3% | | at least 90% |
| Horizontal agreement (pooled) | 100.0% | 77.8% | | at least 90% |
| Failures | 0 | 0 | | 0 |
| Through titles | 2 | 2 | 2 | |
| Reversals | 2 | 1 | 2 | |
| Mean detour (per fixture) | 1.10, 1.38, 1.00, 1.15 | 1.01, 1.09, 1.00, 1.03 | 1.09, 1.37, 1.00, 1.15 | |

The one disagreeing pair is in `er-long-labels`: Mermaid's `CUSTOMER_…` and `P` are both about 80px tall and their centres sit 1px apart; Siren draws an entity with no attributes 48px tall (ADR-0004's padding) beside `P` at 96px, tops aligned in their layer, so the centres sit 24px apart and the pair reads as above/below.

The gate passes. The other kinds are unchanged: the 11 flowchart fixtures (crossings 176 against 176, vertical 99.6%, horizontal 97.8%, through-nodes 0, through-titles 15), the three class fixtures (0 crossings against 0, 97.3% / 100%) and the four state fixtures (0 against 0, 100% / 98.5%).

## Consequences

Every ER diagram's picture changes: orthogonal rounded relationships with line hops, frames from the engine, Mermaid's block order, and a block that names no direction inside one that keeps its own laid out in the enclosing block's direction (it used to take the document's). No diagram kind is laid out by the dagre core any more; removing it is the migration's last step.
